page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is a general-purpose instance type built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network interfaces with a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression registering in the bottom 10%. However, the 24 physical cores compensate in parallel tasks, elevating multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench, and bzip3 decompression benchmarks to average levels. Memory bandwidth also performs in the middle 50% tier, reaching 983.75 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 90.83 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is its reliance on older Intel Broadwell architecture, which limits single-threaded execution speeds and lacks modern instruction sets like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of dedicated physical cores and balanced memory allocation, making it a viable option for parallelized workloads that do not require high single-core clock speeds or local NVMe storage.

This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. It also supports light LLM inference for smaller models, though text generation speeds remain modest.
